nodes.title: python-sdk issue #577: RuntimeError: Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task (out-of-order cleanup)
google/adk-python issue #3708: MCP cancel scope error

nodes.text: MCP Python SDK stdio_client shutdown (_stop_server_process): close the server's stdin, wait PROCESS_TERMINATION_TIMEOUT = 2.0 s for it to exit on its own, then kill the whole process tree (SIGTERM to the process group, SIGKILL after FORCE_KILL_TIMEOUT = 2.0 s; Windows Job Object). The server is spawned in its own session/process group (POSIX) or Job Object (Windows), so descendants are killed too. A process that survives the kill is logged and abandoned, so an orphan is still possible in that last case.
nodes.applicability: Current main branch of the SDK; older releases used a different, shorter sequence and the exact version where the process-group kill landed was not checked.
nodes.limitations: Source summary came through a fetch tool that paraphrased the code; quotes are from that output. Not checked against a pinned release.

nodes.text: The anyio cancel-scope 'different task' error arises when an async context (task group / cancel scope, e.g. inside stdio_client or an AsyncExitStack) is exited from a different asyncio task than the one that entered it, typically a cleanup task calling AsyncExitStack.aclose(); anyio's wrong-task guard raises before removing the host task from the scope. Out-of-order (non-LIFO) cleanup of several clients is a second trigger reported in #577.
nodes.applicability: MCP Python SDK stdio/HTTP clients on asyncio+anyio; reported in python-sdk, Google ADK.
nodes.limitations: No upstream python-sdk maintainer states a recommended pattern; #577 is still open with no confirmed fix; the #577 root cause is a commenter's opinion that another commenter disputed. Reports of FastMCP and langchain-mcp-adapters were not fetched.

nodes.text: Recommended pattern: have one dedicated long-lived owner task enter and exit the MCP client context (connect, serve requests via messages, cleanup), instead of entering in the request task and exiting elsewhere. Google ADK's maintainer called this the architectural root-cause fix (PR #4025, merged in v1.23.0, per the thread); the symptom-only fix was PR #3835.
nodes.limitations: Taken from one maintainer comment in an ADK issue; the python-sdk itself gives no official pattern.

nodes.text: Pydantic-AI's MCP toolset (main) exposes init_timeout (initial connection plus initialize handshake; default 5 s) and read_timeout (max wait for new messages on the long-lived connection; default 5 minutes).
nodes.applicability: The fetched main-branch file documents MCPToolset; MCPServerStdio was not found there, so the defaults for the older MCPServerStdio class were not confirmed from source.
nodes.limitations: Defaults are _UNSET sentinels resolved at runtime to 5 and 5*60, as reported by the fetch tool's summary rather than a verbatim line.

nodes.text: OpenAI Agents SDK MCPServerStdio takes client_session_timeout_seconds: float | None = 5, forwarded to ClientSession as the read timeout (per-request); None and 0 disable it. In the SDK's v2 path the client runs in its own asyncio task.
